title: Official name
decision: TopShelf Operating System is the official product name; TOS is the short name.

title: Product type
decision: TOS is a project operating system, not merely a template or kernel.

title: Repository
decision: The core repository is named topshelf-operating-system.

title: Implementation baseline
decision: TypeScript, Node.js 20+, and pnpm are the default implementation stack.

title: Canonical state
decision: Canonical project state is YAML under .tos; SQLite is a rebuildable derived index.

title: Contract completeness
decision: Every catalog contract is evaluated as required, conditional, or not_applicable with reason.

title: Truth model
decision: Project answers are evidence-backed records, not plain booleans.

title: Interaction model
decision: TOS inspects first, asks only unresolved questions, and defaults conservatively on material uncertainty.

title: Human authority
decision: Patrick retains final risk, external authorization, promotion, financial, and merge authority unless delegated.

title: Agent separation
decision: Implementers may not approve their own work; review and evidence verification are separate functions.

title: Evidence classes
decision: Automated, local manual, deployed/delivered, and external approval evidence remain distinct.

title: Promotion
decision: Lifecycle labels may change only through the promotion controller and required evidence.

title: Teach strategy
decision: Teach remains the product reference; migration uses bounded strangler slices, not a blind rewrite.

title: Learning loop
decision: Project lessons must be evaluated for propagation into reusable TOS controls.
